Subject: Renewal: stair-stepped uplift + fallback ops for co-term

Hi Carl —

Thanks again for the time last week. As Finlytics approaches the September renewal, I wanted to surface a pragmatic path we think will balance your mid-contract growth needs with procurement constraints: a stair-stepped uplift tied to usage bands, with an operational fallback that preserves latency SLOs if usage spikes before the next step.

Key proposal (high level):
- 3-step uplift across the 12-month term: 0–5M tokens (current baseline), 5M–20M tokens (step 1), 20M+ tokens (step 2).
- Step pricing is committed capacity with an annualized discount ladder (higher bands -> higher discount).
- If utilization exceeds the current step and the customer elects to burst, Redwood will route excess requests to a compatible model variant with slightly higher per-token cost but strict latency guarantees (this is the "fallback ops").

Benefits for Finlytics: predictable unit economics during normal growth and a clear, SLA-backed safety net during spikes.

I attached a short proposal and last month's usage export so you have the numbers. Can you confirm your procurement window and whether Finlytics needs co-term alignment with any other vendor contracts? If co-terming is required we'll add a proration clause into the SOW.

Open to scheduling 30m next week to walk finance/procurement through the mechanics.

Thanks,
Rachel

3) For the fallback model variant, will responses be identical enough for our monitoring? We run QA diffs on generated content and need to bound drift.

Hi Carl —

Great questions. Quick answers up front, more detail below and we can cover any of this in Tue's call:

1) Prepay uplift: We can offer a 4.5% prepay discount on step 1 for a full 12-month prepayment. I pushed to get 5% but the margin bins are tight; 4.5% is our best up-front offer without shifting to a multi-year commitment.

2) Proration/Co-term: We use day-level proration on committed units with the option to annualize mid-term (convert remaining term into annualized credit toward the new co-term). We'll include an example clause in the SOW and a sample invoice calculation.

3) Fallback model drift: The fallback variant is a lightly quantized 7B-compatible variant we use for spikes; we guarantee pattern-preserving behaviour for prompts we've profiled (completion length, key token presence). We'll also provide a small diff-report endpoint and a test harness you can run against a canonical prompt set. If you need byte-for-byte parity there's an add-on (dedicated burst lane) we can discuss.

For the Tue 8/18 slot at 2:30pm PT I blocked 30m. Jordan, Ben — can you join to cover legal/billing ops and any credit/discount flexibility? Irene, I included you for SLO escalation path notes.

Thanks,
Rachel
